evidence.quote: This will enable us to assess more data as we move the policy rate closer to a sufficiently restrictive level, taking into account the risks around our dual-mandate goals.
policy will need to be sufficiently restrictive for some time to make sure inflation returns to 2 percent on a sustained basis.
it is likely that the full effect on demand, employment, and inflation of the cumulative tightening that is in the pipeline still lies ahead.
Recent declines in average weekly hours, temporary-help services, and monthly payrolls growth suggest tentative signs that labor demand is cooling.
may provide some reassurance that we are not currently experiencing a 1970s‑style wage–price spiral.
In parallel, balance sheet runoff is continuing.

parsed.rationale: The speech commits to sufficiently restrictive policy but emphasizes disinflation, cooling labor demand, lagged effects of tightening still to come, and a slower pace of hikes, giving a balanced-to-slightly-dovish lean. Inflation is described as high but declining with reassurance about wage-price dynamics.
